domain.name: Web & Product Delivery
domain.description: Practical requirements, frontend/backend engineering, testing, releases, debugging, analytics, and product prioritization.

competencies.name: Requirements & Acceptance Criteria
competencies.description: Translate user goals into testable product requirements.
competencies.purpose: Translate user goals into testable product requirements.

units.title: Requirements & Acceptance Criteria: core principle
units.content: A requirement should be specific enough that two people can independently determine whether it is satisfied.

units.title: Requirements & Acceptance Criteria: working procedure
units.content: State user, problem, desired outcome, constraints, non-goals, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and dependencies before implementation.

units.title: Requirements & Acceptance Criteria: common failures
units.content: Avoid feature lists with no user outcome, hidden assumptions, and acceptance criteria added only after development.

drills.title: Practice Requirements & Acceptance Criteria
drills.prompt: Write acceptance criteria for an event gallery that shows a slideshow when no video exists and preserves load-more state after deletion.

competencies.name: Frontend Engineering
competencies.description: Build responsive interfaces with clear state, accessibility, and maintainable components.
competencies.purpose: Build responsive interfaces with clear state, accessibility, and maintainable components.

units.title: Frontend Engineering: core principle
units.content: Loading, empty, error, success, and disabled states are part of the product design.

units.title: Frontend Engineering: working procedure
units.content: Map states; build semantic structure; define reusable components; implement responsive behavior; add accessibility; test with real content and failures.

units.title: Frontend Engineering: common failures
units.content: Avoid giant components, duplicated styling, inaccessible controls, and layouts tested at only one size.

drills.title: Practice Frontend Engineering
drills.prompt: Outline component/state architecture for a site-content admin editor with preview, saving, and recoverable errors.

competencies.name: Backend & API Design
competencies.description: Design server endpoints with explicit contracts, validation, errors, and permissions.
competencies.purpose: Design server endpoints with explicit contracts, validation, errors, and permissions.

units.title: Backend & API Design: core principle
units.content: APIs are contracts: inputs, outputs, validation, idempotency, permissions, and side effects should be explicit.

units.title: Backend & API Design: working procedure
units.content: Define resource/action; auth; request schema; validation; response schema; failure cases; idempotency; audit needs; versioning implications.

units.title: Backend & API Design: common failures
units.content: Avoid accepting arbitrary fields silently, returning success for failure, leaking stack traces, and undocumented side effects.

drills.title: Practice Backend & API Design
drills.prompt: Design a booking API with validation, duplicate protection, clear errors, and audit data.

competencies.name: Software Testing & QA
competencies.description: Verify behavior across normal, edge, failure, and regression cases.
competencies.purpose: Verify behavior across normal, edge, failure, and regression cases.

units.title: Software Testing & QA: core principle
units.content: Prioritize tests where failure can lose money, data, permissions, or core workflow reliability.

units.title: Software Testing & QA: working procedure
units.content: Identify critical flows; write happy/failure cases; test boundaries; add unit/integration/e2e coverage where useful; reproduce bugs; add regression tests.

units.title: Software Testing & QA: common failures
units.content: Avoid only happy-path testing, flaky timing assumptions, unrealistic test data, and bug fixes without regression coverage.

drills.title: Practice Software Testing & QA
drills.prompt: Create tests for payment success, decline, duplicate submission, timeout, callback retry, and mismatched amount.

competencies.name: Release & Deployment
competencies.description: Ship software with versioning, rollback, verification, and change control.
competencies.purpose: Ship software with versioning, rollback, verification, and change control.

units.title: Release & Deployment: core principle
units.content: A deployment is not complete until critical user workflows are verified.

units.title: Release & Deployment: working procedure
units.content: Build from a known commit; run tests; capture version; protect database/migrations; deploy; smoke test; monitor; retain rollback path.

units.title: Release & Deployment: common failures
units.content: Avoid uncommitted releases, irreversible migrations without backup, configuration drift, and declaring success before smoke tests.

drills.title: Practice Release & Deployment
drills.prompt: Define a safe local FREEOS release checklist from pull through build, database protection, startup, smoke test, and rollback.

competencies.name: Observability & Debugging
competencies.description: Use reproducible evidence to understand and fix software failures.
competencies.purpose: Use reproducible evidence to understand and fix software failures.

units.title: Observability & Debugging: core principle
units.content: Preserve the earliest reliable symptom and change one thing at a time.

units.title: Observability & Debugging: working procedure
units.content: Reproduce; capture exact error/input; reduce scope; inspect logs/state; form one hypothesis; make one change; retest; document root cause and prevention.

units.title: Observability & Debugging: common failures
units.content: Avoid changing many variables, clearing logs before reading them, and shipping workarounds with unknown side effects.

drills.title: Practice Observability & Debugging
drills.prompt: Diagnose a TypeScript build failure using the compiler error, recent diff, targeted fix, rebuild, and regression test.

competencies.name: Product Analytics
competencies.description: Measure whether software features improve user outcomes and workflow efficiency.
competencies.purpose: Measure whether software features improve user outcomes and workflow efficiency.

units.title: Product Analytics: core principle
units.content: Clicks are not the same as value; measure task completion, failure, friction, latency, and retention around real user goals.

units.title: Product Analytics: working procedure
units.content: Define funnel steps; success/failure events; useful properties; privacy limits; baseline; review cadence; compare before/after changes.

units.title: Product Analytics: common failures
units.content: Avoid tracking everything, collecting sensitive data unnecessarily, and optimizing a local metric that harms the overall workflow.

drills.title: Practice Product Analytics
drills.prompt: Define metrics for whether a first-time FREEOS user can understand Start Here, ask a task, use project context, and complete an approval.

competencies.name: Product Prioritization
competencies.description: Choose what to build using value, risk, effort, dependencies, and strategic fit.
competencies.purpose: Choose what to build using value, risk, effort, dependencies, and strategic fit.

units.title: Product Prioritization: core principle
units.content: Foundational reliability and reusable infrastructure can create more leverage than another visible feature.

units.title: Product Prioritization: working procedure
units.content: List candidates; score user impact, mission fit, urgency, risk reduction, effort, dependencies, reversibility, and opportunity cost; sequence the smallest coherent set.

units.title: Product Prioritization: common failures
units.content: Avoid ranking only by excitement, ignoring maintenance cost, and starting many dependent features at once.

drills.title: Practice Product Prioritization
drills.prompt: Rank five FREEOS roadmap items and explain sequencing based on value, reliability, effort, and dependencies.
